verdict.rationale: Mastra documents per-tool approval gating (`requireApproval: true` with an approve/decline stream chunk) and a code mode that runs multi-tool computations in an isolated sandbox, so the agent's own capabilities cover both halves of the story. Both are thin, single-line mentions: approval gating is not a fine-grained permission model, and the sandbox is limited to code mode. Missing for 10: a fine-grained tool permission/allowlist policy model (scopes, per-user or per-agent tool access), documented sandbox isolation details and limits for general tool execution, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can restrict what an agent may do with fine-grained tool permissions and sandboxed execution

citations.quote: Mark a tool with `requireApproval: true`, then check for the `tool-call-approval` chunk in the stream to approve or decline the action
Code mode lets an agent run multi-tool computations in an isolated sandbox and return the result as a single, more accurate response.
Processors transform, validate, or control messages as they pass through an agent.
